The petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking to award compensation of Rs.18,00,000/- for the grievous injuries sustained Vasantha Lakshmi R vs Raghavendra Rao K R on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77001881/

2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
On 27.06.2023 at about 3.15 pm., petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on a motor cycle bearing Reg No.KA-04-EN-0538, which was ridden by Gurumurthy C.,
on the left side of the road, carefully and cautiously.

When they were proceeding in front of Fabritex shop, 1 st main road, Laggere, Bengaluru City, at that time, suddenly the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-Z-8704 came in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering to human life without observing any traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to which the petitioner and rider were fell down and the petitioner sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Chard Road Hospital, Basaveshwar SCCH - 26 3 MVC No.6777/2023 Nagar, Bangalore, wherein after first aid, she was shifted to Apollo Hospital, Sheshadripuram, Bengaluru, for further treatment, wherein she was admitted as an inpatient from 27.06.2023 to 03.07.2023 for 8 days and she has spent Rs.4,00,000/- towards medicine and Rs.50,000/- towards incidental expenses.
The petitioner has undergone operation and she was discharged with an advise to take continues follow-up treatment, as such she has taken treatment as an outpatient.
3. Further the petitioner has stated that, at the time of accident, she was hale and healthy and was doing tailor work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

Due to the injuries sustained in the accident,
she is not able to do her work and lost income, she is suffering from pain, unable to life weight,
stand, sit and squat and she is suffering from mental difficulties and hardship.

Further she has stated that in relation to accident, the Rajajinagar Traffic Police have registered the case in Cr.No.300/2023 against the driver of car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IPC.
The respondent is the R.C. owner of SCCH - 26 4 MVC No.6777/2023 offending Car is liable to pay compensation.
Hence, she has prayed to award compensation from the respondent.
4. After service of summons, the respondent has not appeared before the court and hence, he has been placed exparte.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following points arise for my consideration:
POINTS 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, on 27.06.2023 at about 3.15 pm., when she was proceeding on the motor cycle bearing reg No.KA-04- EN-0538 as a pillion rider on the left side of the road, in front of Fabritex shop, 1st main road,
Laggere, Bengaluru City, at that time, suddenly the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-Z-8704 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the above said motorcycle, as a result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injury, as mentioned in claim petition ?

If so, from which respondent?
3.
What Order or Award?
In order to prove her case, the petitioner has examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20.
The petitioner examined the Medical record officer of Apollo Hospital as PW.2 and got marked 7 documents as Ex.P.21 to Ex.P.27.
7. Heard the argument of learned counsel for the Petitioner.
Perused the entire materials available on records.

8. My findings to the above Points are as under:
Point No.1 : In the Affirmative Point No.2 : Partly in the affirmative Point No.3 : As per final order for the following:
REASONS 9. POINT No.1:- In order to prove the actionable negligence, the petitioner has got examined herself as PW.1.
P.W.1 has reiterated the petition averments in his affidavit by way of examination in chief.
In support of her evidence, she has got marked 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to P.20.
In order to prove point No.1, P.W.1 has produced documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12.

Out of which, Ex.P.1 is the FIR,
Ex.P.2 is SCCH - 26 6 MVC No.6777/2023 the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the spot panchanama, Ex.P.4 is the hand sketch map, Ex.P.5 is the notice U/Sec.133 of M.V. Act, Ex.P.6 is the reply to notice U/Sec.133 of M.V. Act, Ex.P.7 is the MVA report, Ex.P.8 is the wound certificate, Ex.P.9 is the final report, Ex.P.10 to Ex.
P.12 are the statements of witnesses.
The oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner proves that, there was an accident in which she has sustained injuries.

10. On perusal of complaint produced as Ex.P.2 reveals that petitioner's husband has lodged the complaint and on the basis of the complaint, Rajajinagar traffic police have registered FIR as per Ex.P.1 against the driver of the offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-Z-8704.
As per Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.4, the police have conducted panchanama and hand sketch map at the spot of accident.
Ex . P.5
reveals that, the said accident was not due to any mechanical defect of the vehicles.
Ex.P.8 shows that, the petitioner has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident.

The I.O has filed charge sheet as per Ex.P.9 against the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-Z-8704 after completion of SCCH - 26 7 MVC No.6777/2023 investigation based on the evidence available at the spot.

But as per EX.P-1 FIR, EX.P-2 compliant,EX.P-4 Hand sketch map, EX.P-5 Notice U/sec.133 of MV Act, EX.P-6 reply notice U/sec.133 of MV Act, EX.P-7 is the MVA report and Ex.P-10 to 12 witness statements, it shows the offending vehicle number is mentioned as KA-05-Z-8704, but police have mentioned the vehicle number in the final report and panchanma is mentioned as KA-05-Z-8705, but material documents, i,e compliant, FIR , hand sketch map, MVA report, notice, reply notice and MVA report,
Vasantha Lakshmi R vs Raghavendra Rao K R on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77001881/
3

it is clearly shows that the offending vehicle number KA-05/Z-8704.
11.
All the records indicate the negligence on the part of driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-Z-8704.
In this case the respondent remained absent and he has been placed Ex- parte.
Hence, the allegations of the petitioner with regard to negligent driving of offending Car remained unchallenged.

By the above materials and evidence it is clear that the Petitioner has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident due to rash and negligent driving of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-Z-8704 by its driver.
Hence, Point No.1 is SCCH - 26 8 MVC No.6777/2023 answered in the Affirmative.
12. POINT NO.2 :The Petitioner states that due to the accident, she has sustained the grievous injuries.

Immediately she was taken first aid treatment at Chord road Hospital Basaveshwar Nagar Bengaluru and shifted to Apollo Hospitals Sheshadripuram Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as inpatient for a period of seven days, wherein she was treated and discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment regularly.

entities.text: Chord road Hospital Basaveshwar Nagar Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: She has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards hospital charges, medicines, conveyance and attendance charges.

13. It is the contention of the petitioner that, she was aged about 42 years as on the date of accident and doing Tailoring work, due to the accidental injuries, she cannot doing the tailoring work and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries often she gets pain in her body due to which she is unable to carrying out her daily day today activities.

14. So far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, SCCH - 26 9 MVC No.6777/2023 the Petitioner has sought for compensation of Rs.18,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in road traffic accident.
15. In the instant case the petitioner has not examined doctor to prove the degree of her disability.
As already stated supra, absolutely there is nothing on record to show the extent of disability of petitioner caused due to accident.
Therefore, in the absence of any evidence to that effect, this Tribunal is not inclined to accept the version of the petitioner that she is having permanent disability caused in the accident.
16. The petitioner has not examined the doctor and there is no disability certificate.

As per guidelines issued by the Central Government for the purpose of assessing the extent of specified disability in a person included under the rights of persons with disability Act 2016 dated 04-01- 2018, the injuries sustained by the petitioner are not come under the any disability.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore, the injuries sustained by the petitioner do not cause any disability for the SCCH - 26 10 MVC No.6777/2023 petitioner's body or part of the body.
However, in view of the injury sustained by her in the accident she had suffered pain.
17. So far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the Petitioner has sought for compensation of Rs.18,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in road traffic accident.
The PW1 has produced Ex.P15 - medical bills amounting to Rs.20,969/- to show the expenses incurred by her.

sentences.text: The petitioner has contended that due to accident she has sustained grievous injuries.
In order to prove the injuries caused to her, she has produced Ex.P.8 wound certificate and Ex.P.13 and 14 discharge summary.

On perusal of Ex.P.8 it is clear that the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
1) B/L forearm fracture (Both bone), Abrasion over left feet (Dorsal and Lateral skin)1x2 cm and abrasion over the right shoulder 1x1cm
The doctor opines that all the injuries are grievous in nature.

As per Ex.P.13 and 14 - discharge summary issued SCCH - 26 11 MVC No.6777/2023 by Apollo Hospital and CITI Hospital, which discloses that, she took treatment from 27-06-2023 to 03-07-2023 and 23- 08-2024 to 26-08-2024 i.e., for 11 days, which discloses that on examination it was found - Petitioner was admitted with history of RTA, on clinical examination and investigation were done.
But there are no evidences that, the Petitioner is suffering from any difficulties which would affect her livelihood and day-today activities and earning capacity.
In the absence of medical evidence to prove disability, I deem it proper to award global compensation.

By considering the nature of injuries, age of the petitioner, treatment taken in the hospital as stated supra and considering the pain and sufferings by the Petitioner, I deem it appropriate to award Rs.1,50,000/- as global compensation under all the conventional heads with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

19. Regarding Interest & Liability: Even after service of notice, the Respondent has remained absent and hence the evidence lead by the petitioner is remained unchallenged.
SCCH - 26 12 MVC No.6777/2023 Therefore, the respondent is the RC owner of offending motor cycle and is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly, I answer Point No.2 in the 'Partly affirmative'.
20. POINT NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
-: ORDER :-
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms:
The petitioner is entitled for a compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
The respondent is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
